title: dream
content_html:
dream

In Nerve, the speaker dreams of travelling to a desert. Near the end, a desert scene carries the feeling of having lived there. In dream sleep, the word dream also means an aspiration, and a lost ball bearing is vividly remembered. An invented place, a recollection and a wish can inhabit the same scene. What gives such a scene the feeling of somewhere we have been, and why can that feeling outlast the details? Nerve · dream sleep

Reading note. Jung and Daoism. Jung follows images across a series of dreams in Psychology and Alchemy. The butterfly story in the Zhuangzi turns on a different question about who is dreaming whom. Both offer ways into the recurring place in Nerve. What becomes familiar across its appearances, and whose experience do we take that familiarity to be? Psychology and Alchemy, part II, §§44–50 · Zhuangzi, 2
